Hi Alicia / MedSync security team,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed set of next steps so we stay aligned while your engineering and security teams evaluate a Private deployment (VPC / on-prem / air-gapped options).

Summary from the call:
- Goal: host Redwood Inference runtime on your infrastructure with network isolation and control over data residency.
- Compliance drivers: HIPAA for PHI in some workloads, GDPR for EU customers, and an upcoming vendor security review.
- Immediate asks: SOC 2 status, a simple network diagram showing border devices and where model inference traffic would terminate, and whether an air-gapped (no internet egress) install is required or optional.

Outstanding items / actions for MedSync (requested):
1) Fill out the quick intake attached (redwood_security_intake_form_v1.pdf) and return to us. It has fields for data classification, expected traffic patterns, and contact info for your infra and network teams.
2) Share your network diagram (even a rough Draw.io export is fine). You mentioned an internal diagram; please send.
3) Confirm SOC 2 status and any existing audit artifacts (Type I/II, dates).
4) Indicate whether you require a fully air-gapped install or if private peering/VPN is acceptable.

What Redwood will do next:
- We will review your answers and prepare an architecture note outlining 2 options: 1) Private VPC with VNet/peering and firewall rules; 2) On-prem air-gapped deployment with physical isolation and HSM/KMS integration.
- Karthik will pick up detailed technical questions around key management and persistent KV cache behavior.
- If agreed, we can schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive next week with your network and security engineers.

Attachments: redwood_security_intake_form_v1.pdf (form)

Would you be able to return the intake and preliminary diagram by end of week (Fri 12 Mar)? That will let us prepare the two architecture variants and a rough effort estimate.

Thanks,

Hi all — thanks for the context, Alicia. Below are concise answers and a proposed next-steps checklist. I have also attached our private deployment checklist for their infra team (redwood_private_deploy_checklist.xlsx).

Short answers to Alicia's questions:
1) Outbound internet access: The runtime can operate with zero outbound egress for model inference. However, by design, automatic model updates and certain telemetry features require outbound access. For air-gapped installs we:
   - Disable automatic model pulls and telemetry by policy.
   - Support manual model bundle transfers (signed tarball) and local installation procedures.
   - Provide a signed verification tool to validate bundle integrity without external calls.

2) KMS and KV/cache encryption:
   - We support integration with customer-managed KMS (local HSM or cloud-hosted KMS) for encryption-at-rest keys.
   - KV cache and persistent prefix caches are encrypted at rest using keys you control. We do not persist plaintext tokens.
   - For air-gapped installs, we recommend a local HSM or KMS appliance; we provide a guide for configuring our runtime to use a local KMS endpoint.

Network isolation options and constraints:
- Option A: Private peering / Direct Connect / VPN
  - Pros: lower operational complexity, supports central KMS via private network if required
  - Cons: requires network ACLs and strict firewalling; egress to the internet may still be possible if misconfigured
- Option B: Fully air-gapped on-prem
  - Pros: maximal isolation, suitable for workloads requiring no external connectivity
  - Cons: manual model updates and patching process; additional operational burden and longer time to onboard

Questions we should ask their infra team in the deep-dive:
- Which subnets will host the inference nodes and where are the upstream routing/firewall devices?
- Do you have an existing HSM/KMS appliance on-prem, and what protocol (PKCS#11, KMIP) does it expose?
- Expected concurrent QPS and peak sequence lengths (tokens) so we can size GPU pools and caching policies.
- Any data egress monitoring or DLP appliances that could interfere with large model weights transfer?

Proposed next steps:
1) Schedule a 60-min technical deep dive with MedSync network and security engineers (we propose Thu or Fri this week).
2) MedSync shares the completed intake and an updated network diagram.
3) Redwood provides the 1-2 page architecture note and the private-deploy checklist (attached).
4) After the deep-dive, we will produce a short SoW/estimate for the chosen path.

Estimate: for a non-air-gapped private peering deployment, 2-3 weeks of integration work (projected). For a fully air-gapped site, 4-6 weeks including validation and manual provisioning steps.

I'll be on the call for the deep dive. If you can confirm a preferred time, I'll send a calendar invite and an agenda.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
